and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$. If $a<b$, assume that $f$ is integrable
([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Then:

1. if $a < b$, the real-valued function $t \mapsto \lVert f(t)\rVert_2$ is
   integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]], [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]);
2. $$\Bigl\lVert \int_a^b f \Bigr\rVert_2 \;\le\; \int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2 .$$

of [[def-oriented-integral]] and
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], interchanging the limits changes
the sign of the right-hand side but not of the left, so for $b < a$ the correct
statement is $\bigl\lVert\int_a^b f\bigr\rVert_2 \le \bigl|\int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2\bigr|$;
the displayed inequality as written is false in that case. This is the same trap
the scalar inequality of

each $f_i$ is integrable does not by itself say that

Fix one mode $m$ and a positive-length closed trial interval $J=[a,b]$ with $a<b$. **Certified hybrid event-enclosure data** consist of the following.

A continuous piecewise dense reconstruction $U$ accumulated from the last reported reset through the current trial prefix, a finite rational residual-tube certificate for the mode ODE launched from that reported reset whose stored reconstruction is exactly $U$, and its returned `certified` status. Write $\eta_{\rm loc}$ for the rational upper bound on the checker-certified distance from $U$ to that exact mode solution over the entire prefix. The soundness interface is [[def-validated-residual-tube-certificate]], [[alg-validated-residual-tube-certificate-checker]], and [[thm-validated-residual-tube-certificate-sound]]. One concrete dense-output formula is [[def-heun-quadratic-dense-output]], but any reconstruction with such a certificate is allowed.

The complete interval root isolation in [F2] finds both roots and classifies their derivative signs. It cannot certify `no event`, because the root at $3/4$ is an enabled event; the earliest enabled event is exactly $3/4$. Thus equal endpoint signs do not justify an event-absence conclusion, while complete root isolation and orientation classification do.
